 Steelers notebook: Mike Tomlin greets several of his former players ahead of ‘Sunday Night Football’ telecast
 By Chris Harlan 3 Min Read 
 • Nov. 15, 2026 
 | 1 minute ago 
-->
 Go Ad-Free today 
 Mike Tomlin relaxes on the set of “Sunday Night Football” before his former team, the Steelers, played the Bengals on Sunday at Paycor Stadium. (Chaz Palla | TribLive) 
 Mike Tomlin (left) speaks during the “Sunday Night Football” pregame show Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, at Paycor Stadium. (Chaz Palla | TribLive) 
 CINCINNATI — Mike Tomlin didn’t mince words while describing the intensity of a Steelers-Bengals rivalry that the former coach knows well. 
 “There’s a nastiness to it,” said Tomlin, a first-year analyst for NBC Sports during Sunday night’s telecast from Paycor Stadium. “There’s genuine bad blood. There will be no jersey swaps after this.” 
 A steady stream of his former players greeted him before kickoff, including Aaron Rodgers and Jalen Ramsey, who were each spotted sharing a hug with Tomlin on the set of “Sunday Night Football.” He also embraced Mike McCarthy, his successor as Steelers coach. Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, Troy Fautanu and Pat Freiermuth, among others, chatted with Tomlin on the field pregame. 
 “Great to see this special group of men again,” Tomlin wrote on the social media. 
 Tomlin was part of the rivalry for 19 seasons as the Steelers’ coach, and his teams typically fared well in the series. He compiled a 28-11 record against the Bengals overall, including a playoff win in 2016. 
 In games at Cincinnati, he went 15-5. 
 But the 54-year-old pointed out how his role nowadays had changed as he covered his first Steelers game as an analyst. 
 “I’m not going to call a play or make a decision tonight,” he said. 
 “Sunday Night Football” is scheduled to visit Pittsburgh on Dec. 6 for a Texans-Steelers game at Acrisure Stadium. 
 Official business 
 Four members of the officiating crew completed an unusual doubleheader Sunday by working two games more than 100 miles apart. 
 Referee Don Willard, umpire Terry Killens, side judge Justin Larrew and field judge Jabir Walker officiated a 1 p.m. game in Indianapolis between the Colts and Miami Dolphins. They then boarded a van for a trip to Cincinnati to officiate the Steelers and Bengals on Sunday night. 
 A nationwide ground stoppage ordered Friday by the Federal Aviation Administration disrupted weekend air travel. The NFL reassigned some officials to work games within driving distance of their homes and asked Willard and his three crew members to pull double duty. 
 Willard usually works as a side judge but took on referee duties Sunday. 
 2-TE formation 
 The Steelers sent out only two captains for the pregame coin toss, and both were tight ends: Darnell Washington and Robert Tonyan. 
 Dance break 
 The Bengals turned to fan favorite Ickey Woods to hype up the Paycor Stadium crowd ahead of kickoff. And, of course, the retired running back performed his iconic “Ickey Shuffle” touchdown dance. 
 Woods, 60, played 37 games over four seasons for the Bengals from 1988-91. His best season was his rookie year, when he rushed for 1,066 yards and 15 touchdowns. 
 Quotable 
 “In the words of the late great ambassador (Dan) Rooney, officials should be like the pylons, meaning they should not be the story,” Tomlin said on the NBC broadcast. “I certainly understand how challenging it is, but they better keep their flags in their pockets tonight and let the players decide the outcome of this football game.” 
 — Tomlin on NBC telecast
